hero.headline: U.S. and Iran reach tentative ceasefire agreement pending Trump approval
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement on a 60-day ceasefire extension, though the deal requires final approval from President Trump. Vice President Vance said the two countries are very close to finalizing the arrangement, describing the negotiations as nearing completion.

According to a U.S. official who spoke with Axios, the proposed deal would include several key components. During the 60-day period, the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened for trade, Iran would be permitted to freely sell oil, and both nations would hold talks on limiting Iran's nuclear program. Iran would also agree to clear mines it has deployed in the strait and refrain from imposing tolls on ships passing through.

In return, the U.S. would lift its blockade on Iranian ports that has been in effect since April 13. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the deal could achieve "a completely open" Strait of Hormuz "without tolls" if successful, though Iranian media has reported that the strait would remain under Iranian control.

The agreement would reportedly unfreeze some Iranian assets held in banks outside Iran. Hostilities would be halted on all fronts, including between Israel and Lebanon.

A senior Iranian source told Reuters that Tehran had not agreed to hand over its highly enriched uranium stockpile. The source stated that Iran's nuclear issue was not part of the preliminary agreement with the U.S., contradicting earlier reporting that Tehran had expressed willingness to give up the stockpile.

The draft plan has been put on the table by both sides, though multiple details remain unconfirmed. Neither government has released comprehensive details about all terms included in the proposed ceasefire. The 60-day timeframe would serve as an initial cooling-off period rather than a permanent end to hostilities.

U.S. officials indicated they are moving closer to a deal despite ongoing military engagement between the nations. The negotiations have progressed even as fighting continues, with officials acknowledging the apparent contradiction between ongoing combat and the diplomatic push toward a ceasefire.

Trump has not yet signed off on the tentative deal. His approval remains the final step before the ceasefire can take effect. Officials did not provide a timeline for when Trump might make a decision on the proposed agreement.

The deal marks a significant development in efforts to halt the conflict between the two nations. It remains possible that some aspects of the agreement could change before final authorization is given.

cards.headline: Netanyahu Orders Israeli Military to Expand Control of Gaza to 70 Percent
cards.teaser: The Israeli prime minister directed the military to increase territorial control in Gaza, a move that would violate the ceasefire terms agreed to in October 2025.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has directed the Israel Defense Forces to expand their control of Gaza to 70 percent of the territory, according to BBC News.

The planned expansion would violate the ceasefire agreement that Israel and Hamas reached in October 2025. That accord set specific restrictions on Israeli military operations and the extent of territorial control within Gaza.

cards.headline: U.S. Officials Say They Are Nearing Deal to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: An emerging framework could set the stage for extending the ceasefire with Iran and opening more substantive negotiations, though President Trump has not yet approved the plan.
cards.body:
U.S. officials say they are closing in on an arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway that has been a focal point of tensions with Iran. The emerging framework has not yet been signed off on by President Trump, according to officials familiar with the negotiations.

The potential agreement could set the table for extending the current ceasefire between the United States and Iran. Officials indicated the arrangement might also open the door to more substantive negotiations between the two countries on broader issues beyond the strait's status.

cards.headline: Russian Drone Hits Apartment Building in NATO Member Romania
cards.body:
A Russian drone struck a residential apartment building in Romania during an overnight attack on Ukraine, injuring two people and sparking swift international condemnation. Romania summoned Russia's ambassador on Friday to denounce what officials described as "irresponsible escalation" by Moscow.

The incident represents the latest example of the Ukraine conflict directly affecting NATO territory. Romania shares a border with Ukraine and has experienced previous instances of military debris crossing into its airspace during the ongoing war.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte responded to the strike by stating that "Russia's reckless behaviour is a danger to us all." The alliance reiterated its commitment to Romania, with the US declaring "We stand with our NATO ally." The response underscored NATO's fundamental principle that an attack on one member constitutes an attack on all.

Romanian President Klaus Iohannis characterized the drone strike as the most serious security incident since the war began, highlighting the escalating nature of spillover effects from the conflict. European officials joined the condemnation, with the European Union saying Russia had crossed "another line" with the attack.

The strike comes amid growing concern among NATO leaders about Russian testing of the alliance's resolve along its eastern border. Czech President Petr Pavel recently called for NATO to "show its teeth" in response to repeated Russian provocations, suggesting a range of options including disconnecting Russian internet access, cutting Russian banks from global financial systems, and shooting down aircraft that violate allied airspace. Pavel advocated for "decisive enough, potentially even asymmetric" responses to counter Moscow's behavior.

Estonian and Latvian officials have noted that Ukrainian drones have been appearing in Baltic airspace, which they attribute to Russian electronic jamming pushing the weapons off course during operations against Russian targets. Estonia's foreign minister stated that the only reason Ukrainian drones were entering Estonian territory was due to Russian electronic warfare diverting them from their intended routes.

Ukraine's foreign ministry spokesman expressed regret for such unintended incidents, apologizing to Estonia and Baltic allies. He emphasized that Kyiv had never attempted to use Baltic airspace for its drone operations and had consistently aimed at legitimate targets within Russia. Ukrainian officials blamed Moscow for the electronic jamming causing the diversions.

Baltic leaders have stressed that their nations have not permitted their airspace to be used for launching or conducting attacks against Russia. They have maintained close communication with Ukrainian counterparts regarding drone operations, requesting that Ukrainian forces adjust their trajectories to stay as far as possible from NATO territory given Russian jamming capabilities.

The incident underscores the growing friction between NATO and Russia as the Ukraine conflict continues, with European officials warning that such provocations risk further destabilizing the region.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Designates Brazilian Drug Gangs as Terrorist Groups
cards.teaser: Following through on threats and a push by the Bolsonaro family, the U.S. has labeled Brazil's two largest drug gangs as terrorist organizations.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has designated Brazil's two largest drug gangs as terrorist groups, following through on previous threats to take such action. The move came after a new push by members of the Bolsonaro family for the United States to classify the criminal organizations as terrorist entities.

The designation applies to the two most powerful drug trafficking organizations operating in Brazil. The terrorist label carries significant legal and financial implications, potentially affecting how U.S. law enforcement and intelligence agencies can target the groups and their financial networks.

cards.headline: Europe Moves Toward Trade Conflict With China
cards.teaser: European officials are urgently seeking solutions as an influx of cheap Chinese goods threatens the continent's manufacturing base.
cards.body:
European policymakers intensified their search for responses to a flood of low-cost Chinese imports that have put pressure on domestic manufacturers. The volume of goods entering European markets has raised concerns about the viability of local production.

The situation has prompted discussions about potential trade barriers or other measures to protect European industry. Officials described the search for solutions as increasingly urgent as the gap between Chinese and European production costs continues to widen. The developments suggest Europe may be moving toward a more confrontational trade posture with China.

cards.headline: Dell Wins $9.7 Billion Pentagon Contract
cards.teaser: The defense department awarded Dell Technologies a major contract to streamline software purchases after company founder Michael Dell developed ties with the Trump administration.
cards.body:
Dell Technologies secured a $9.7 billion contract from the Pentagon to handle software procurement. The award came after company founder Michael Dell established an early relationship with President Trump, meeting with him during the transition period.

Trump acquired stock in Dell and publicly praised the company before the contract announcement. The deal allows the Defense Department to consolidate its software purchasing through Dell's services. The contract represents one of the largest technology awards to a single vendor in recent Pentagon history.

cards.headline: UN Adds Israel and Russia to Sexual Violence Blacklist
cards.teaser: Israeli and Russian forces were added to the United Nations blacklist for sexual violence in conflict zones, prompting Israel to sever ties with the UN chief.
cards.body:
The United Nations added Israel and Russia to its blacklist of parties that have committed sexual violence in conflict zones. The designation places both countries on the same list as Hamas and other groups accused of conflict-related sexual violence.

Israel responded by announcing it would cut ties with UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres over the inclusion. Israeli officials accused the UN of placing Israel on the same sexual violence blacklist as Hamas, which Israel designates as a terrorist organization. Russia and Israel join other state and non-state actors on the UN list documenting sexual violence in armed conflicts.

cards.headline: Mother-in-Law of Indian Bride Arrested After Death Sparks Media Frenzy
cards.teaser: The mother-in-law of Twisha Sharma has been arrested following the bride's death on May 12, which sparked rival claims of murder and suicide.
cards.body:
The mother-in-law of Twisha Sharma has been arrested following the bride's death on May 12. The case has dominated Indian headlines and sparked significant public attention.

Sharma's death has generated conflicting claims between different parties, with some alleging murder while others suggest suicide. The arrest marks a major development in an investigation that has drawn intense media scrutiny across India.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes During Test at Cape Canaveral
cards.teaser: A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on a launch pad in Florida during a test.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on the launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night during an engine-firing test. The incident occurred ahead of a satellite launch that had been planned for the following week.

Blue Origin, the space company founded by Jeff Bezos, was conducting the test when the explosion happened at the launch facility.

cards.teaser: A rocket belonging to Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin exploded on the launch pad during a test ahead of a planned satellite launch.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on the launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida during an engine-firing test on Thursday night. The explosion occurred ahead of a satellite launch that had been scheduled for the following week.

The rocket belonged to Jeff Bezos' space company Blue Origin. The test was intended to verify engine performance before the planned launch.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer says she will not run for president in 2028
cards.teaser: Democratic Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced she will not seek the presidency in 2028.
cards.body:
Governor Gretchen Whitmer of Michigan stated she will not be a candidate for president in the 2028 election. The Democratic governor made the announcement, removing herself from speculation about potential contenders for the next presidential race.

Whitmer later walked back aspects of her comment about not running in 2028, according to reports. The governor had been considered among potential Democratic candidates for the next presidential cycle.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The Department of Justice has begun an investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault.
cards.body:
The Justice Department opened an investigation into E. Jean Carroll, according to reports. Carroll previously accused Donald Trump of sexual assault and won civil cases against him.

The DOJ investigation represents a new development in the long-running legal disputes between Carroll and Trump.

cards.headline: 14-year-old Shrey Parikh wins Scripps National Spelling Bee
cards.teaser: Shrey Parikh won the 101st Scripps National Spelling Bee after a rapid-fire spell-off round.
cards.body:
Shrey Parikh, 14, from California, won the 101st Scripps National Spelling Bee in a dramatic tiebreaker against fellow competitor Ishaan Gupta. As the favorite heading into the competition, Parikh demonstrated his confidence throughout the final round.

The champion's victory came down to a 90-second "spell-off," a rapid-fire format introduced in 2021. Parikh dominated the tiebreaker, correctly spelling 32 words compared to Gupta's 25. This marks the third time the national competition has been decided by the spell-off format.

cards.headline: Becerra leads California governor's race as primary approaches
cards.teaser: Former Attorney General Xavier Becerra holds the lead in polling for California's gubernatorial race, with Rick Hilton and Tom Steyer competing for second place.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra leads the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom in California, according to a new poll. Rick Hilton and Tom Steyer are in a tight contest for the second spot in the state's primary election.

The poll shows Becerra opening a lead over other Democratic candidates in the packed field. California uses a top-two primary system where all candidates compete on the same ballot regardless of party affiliation.

cards.headline: Two charged after woman fatally shot outside Sheffield bar
cards.teaser: Two people have been charged after Shanice Brookes, 30, was shot and killed outside a bar in Sheffield.
cards.body:
Shanice Brookes, 30, died after being shot outside a bar in Sheffield, England. Police described her as an innocent bystander in the shooting.

Two individuals have been charged in connection with the killing. The shooting occurred outside a bar, where Brookes was present when the gunfire erupted.

hero.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes on Florida Launch Pad
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night, destroying the launch pad in a massive fireball. The explosion occurred at 9pm ET during what was scheduled as a routine engine-firing test before the rocket's planned satellite launch.

The blast was visible for miles along Florida's Atlantic coast. An orange sky was reported in Fort Pierce, 185 kilometers south of the launch site, and shockwaves were felt across the space coast region. Residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reported their homes shaking, while people in South Carolina, hundreds of miles away, reported seeing a glow in the sky. Flames continued burning at the launch pad for more than two hours after the explosion.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed that all employees were safe and uninjured. He acknowledged the incident on social media, saying "It's a very rough day" and added that while it was too early to determine the root cause, the company was already investigating. "We'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying," Bezos wrote.

The explosion carries significant consequences for NASA's lunar program. NASA had announced just two days earlier that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three planned uncrewed missions this year to begin construction of a $20 billion lunar base. The New Glenn rocket is the vehicle NASA intends to use for these missions, including launching landers that will eventually transport astronauts to the moon's surface.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency would conduct a full evaluation of the timeline for the Artemis program following the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he stated. NASA indicated it would work with Blue Origin to support a thorough investigation and assess the impact on near-term missions.

This represents the latest in a series of setbacks for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for NASA contracts. Last month, a payload from the New Glenn's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the rocket to return to flight the previous week.

The explosion also affects Blue Origin's competition with SpaceX for the Artemis program. Both companies have built new facilities at Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions. NASA plans to test both Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander and SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System during the Artemis III mission in 2027 to determine which will carry astronauts to the lunar surface in the subsequent Artemis IV mission scheduled for 2028.

SpaceX founder Elon Musk commented briefly on the incident, saying "Most unfortunate" and noting that "Rockets are hard."

cards.headline: Mortgage Rates Climb to Nine-Month High
cards.teaser: The average rate on long-term US mortgages rose to 6.53 percent, the highest level since last summer.
cards.body:
Average long-term mortgage rates have reached 6.53 percent, the highest level seen in nine months. This increase has made home purchases less affordable for prospective buyers across the country.

Many homebuyers have shifted their expectations, abandoning hopes for lower rates and adjusting their purchasing plans accordingly. Despite the higher rates, housing markets continue to show activity rather than freezing entirely, though the market remains pressured by limited inventory and elevated home prices.

cards.headline: Markets React to Potential US-Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices and stock markets fluctuated as investors weighed signs of a possible deal to extend a cease-fire.
cards.body:
Financial markets fluctuated as the United States and Iran moved closer to extending their cease-fire agreement. Oil prices remained volatile, declining at times as traders monitored progress on negotiations. Stock indexes also showed sensitivity to developments in the talks.

US officials confirmed that the framework for a cease-fire extension had been agreed upon, pending approval from Trump and Iran's leadership. Vice President Vance indicated the two sides were "very close" to a final deal but had not yet reached one. Neither country appeared interested in resuming full-scale conflict, despite recent exchanges of strikes.

cards.headline: ABC Accuses Trump Administration of License Threats
cards.teaser: The television network said the Federal Communications Commission targeted its broadcast station licenses in retaliation.
cards.body:
ABC accused the Trump administration of threatening its broadcast licenses through actions at the Federal Communications Commission. The network called the regulator's conduct an unconstitutional campaign of retaliation against the company.

The allegations suggest the FCC targeted ABC's station licenses in response to the network's coverage or business decisions. ABC characterized the actions as an attempt to pressure the broadcaster through regulatory means. The dispute represents an escalation in tensions between the administration and major media organizations over broadcast licensing authority.

cards.teaser: European officials are urgently seeking solutions as an influx of cheap Chinese goods threatens the continent's manufacturing base.
cards.body:
European policymakers intensified their search for responses to a flood of low-cost Chinese imports that have put pressure on domestic manufacturers. The volume of goods entering European markets has raised concerns about the viability of local production.

The situation has prompted discussions about potential trade barriers or other measures to protect European industry. Officials described the search for solutions as increasingly urgent as the gap between Chinese and European production costs continues to widen. The developments suggest Europe may be moving toward a more confrontational trade posture with China.

cards.headline: BMW Adopts Humanoid Robots for Car Production
cards.teaser: The automaker is deploying humanoid robots at a European plant, expanding on similar efforts in the United States.
cards.body:
BMW announced it is introducing humanoid robots to a car manufacturing facility in Europe as part of its production strategy. The company described humanoid robots as the future of automobile manufacturing.

The European deployment builds on BMW's earlier robot projects at US facilities. The humanoid machines can perform tasks that previously required human workers, though the company has not specified which assembly line jobs the robots will handle. The move reflects growing automation in the automotive industry as manufacturers seek to reduce labor costs and increase production flexibility.

hero.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during test in Florida
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night, destroying the launch pad and dealing a significant blow to the company's plans to support NASA's lunar ambitions.

The massive fireball erupted seconds after the scheduled hotfire test began at 9pm ET at Launch Complex 36. The explosion was so powerful that an orange sky was visible in Fort Pierce, 115 miles to the south, and shockwaves were felt across Florida's space coast. Residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach reported their homes shaking, and people as far north as South Carolina reported seeing the glow in the sky. Blue Origin confirmed that all employees were safe and uninjured.

The timing of the explosion is particularly damaging to Blue Origin's ambitions. Just two days earlier, NASA had selected the company to conduct the first of three uncrewed lunar missions planned for this year to begin construction of a $20 billion moon base. The New Glenn rocket was intended to launch lunar landers for NASA's Artemis program, including landers that would carry astronauts to the moon's surface.

Blue Origin described the incident as an "anomaly" and said it was already investigating the root cause. Company founder Jeff Bezos tweeted that the day was "very rough" but pledged to "rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying."

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman acknowledged the severity of the situation, stating that spaceflight is "unforgiving" and that developing heavy-lift launch capability is "extraordinarily difficult." He said NASA would conduct a full evaluation of how the explosion affects the timeline for the Artemis and moon base programs.

This explosion represents the latest setback for Blue Origin as it competes with Elon Musk's SpaceX for NASA contracts. The company faced previous challenges when a payload from New Glenn's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit last month, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test conducted since the FAA cleared the rocket to return to flight the previous week.

The New Glenn rocket plays a central role in NASA's broader lunar exploration strategy. Beyond the uncrewed missions, Blue Origin is competing with SpaceX to provide the lunar lander for the Artemis IV mission scheduled for 2028, which would see astronauts land on the moon for the first time since 1972.

The investigation into the explosion will likely determine how long the New Glenn program remains grounded and whether NASA's lunar timeline must be adjusted. Blue Origin and SpaceX have both constructed large facilities at Cape Canaveral to support their partnership with NASA on crewed and cargo missions.

cards.headline: AI models accept false information as true despite warnings, study finds
cards.teaser: Large language models continued to treat false statements as accurate even after being explicitly told the information was incorrect.
cards.body:
Researchers found that large language models exhibited bias toward confidently representing claims as true even when warned the statements were false. The finding emerged from fine-tuning tests conducted on AI systems.

The research tested how AI models respond when presented with misinformation alongside warnings about its accuracy. The models demonstrated a tendency to accept and propagate false claims despite explicit corrections, raising concerns about reliability in applications where factual accuracy is essential.

cards.headline: Supermassive black hole discovered without surrounding galaxy
cards.teaser: The James Webb Space Telescope found a black hole that formed before its host galaxy, contradicting current theories.
cards.body:
Scientists discovered a supermassive black hole that exists without an associated galaxy, challenging established understanding of how these cosmic structures form. The discovery was made using the James Webb Space Telescope, which identified the object as a 'little red dot' in the early universe.

The finding contradicts the standard model that galaxies form first and black holes develop at their centers afterward. Researchers have not yet determined how such a black hole could exist in isolation, describing the discovery as a paradigm shift in astrophysics.

cards.headline: Waymo leads autonomous vehicle registrations in Texas as Tesla lags
cards.teaser: A new tracking tool shows Waymo registered significantly more self-driving vehicles in Texas than competitors including Tesla.
cards.body:
Waymo has secured significantly more autonomous vehicle registrations in Texas than Tesla, according to a new state tracking tool. The system offers unprecedented visibility into the scale of robotaxi and self-driving truck operations across the state.

Texas recently enacted legislation establishing the AV tracker to monitor autonomous vehicle deployments. The tool provides the clearest public accounting to date of how many self-driving vehicles are actually operating in the state, revealing Waymo's commanding lead in the competitive autonomous driving market.

cards.headline: Enterprise AI search startup Glean reaches $300 million in annual revenue
cards.teaser: The company tripled its revenue as it positioned AI-powered budget cutting as a major selling point to corporate clients.
cards.body:
Glean crossed $300 million in annual revenue, tripling its top line despite competition from major technology companies entering the enterprise AI search category. The startup attributed growth to positioning its product as a tool for reducing corporate expenses.

The company focused its sales strategy on demonstrating how AI-powered search can help enterprises cut budgets. This approach resonated with customers even as tech giants launched competing products in the same market segment.

cards.headline: Fish-eating dinosaur from 70 million years ago found in Argentina
cards.teaser: Researchers discovered a heron-like dinosaur that fed on fish in the ancient ecosystem.
cards.body:
Scientists identified a new species of dinosaur in Argentina that resembled a heron and ate fish. The creature lived approximately 70 million years ago based on fossil evidence.

The dinosaur's physical structure and feeding behavior paralleled modern wading birds. The discovery adds to understanding of dinosaur diversity in South America during the late Cretaceous period.

cards.headline: Audi releases 2027 RS5 performance hybrid with new electric rear differential
cards.teaser: The vehicle features an entirely new electric torque-vectoring rear differential developed by Audi.
cards.body:
Audi launched the 2027 RS5 as a performance plug-in hybrid equipped with newly engineered technology. The vehicle incorporates an electric torque-vectoring rear differential that Audi developed specifically for this model.

First drive reviews highlighted the car's split personalities, combining electric efficiency with high-performance capabilities. The differential technology represents a new approach to managing power distribution in hybrid performance vehicles.

hero.headline: Four-time Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion known for his aggressive playing style and clutch playoff performances, died Thursday at age 60. According to authorities, Lemieux died by suicide.

The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office responded to a call just after 3 a.m. at a furniture store showroom in Lake Park, Florida, where the victim was believed to be Lemieux.

Lemieux won his four Stanley Cup titles with three different teams throughout his career, establishing himself as one of hockey's most accomplished winners. A fiery winger, Lemieux earned the Conn Smythe Trophy in 1995, awarded to the playoff MVP. His hard-hitting approach to the game angered opponents and sometimes drew attention away from his considerable skill set, but his ability to perform in high-pressure situations made him a valued member of championship rosters.

During his playing career, Lemieux became known as an agitator who combined physical intensity with genuine hockey talent. His competitive nature and winning mentality proved instrumental across multiple championship teams and different eras of professional hockey.

After his playing days ended, Lemieux transitioned into another role within the sport, becoming a player agent and continuing his involvement in professional hockey circles.

The hockey world lost one of its notable champions from the 1980s, 1990s, and 2000s. Lemieux's career demonstrated an exceptional ability to contribute to winning teams over an extended period, with his playoff performances standing out as particularly significant.

His legacy in professional hockey centers on his contributions to four championship-winning rosters across different decades of the game. Though his ferocious style sometimes overshadowed his prodigious skills, Lemieux's impact on the sport as a competitor and later as an agent remained substantial.

cards.headline: Spurs force Game 7 with blowout win over Thunder in Western Conference finals
cards.teaser: Victor Wembanyama scored 28 points as San Antonio dominated Oklahoma City 118-91 to extend the series.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama led the San Antonio Spurs to a decisive 118-91 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Thursday night, forcing a Game 7 in the Western Conference finals. The star player contributed 28 points and 10 rebounds in the dominant home performance.

Facing elimination, the Spurs delivered a commanding blowout to keep their season alive. The series will conclude Saturday in Oklahoma City, with the winner advancing to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks.

cards.headline: World number one Jannik Sinner eliminated from French Open amid heat concerns
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Sinner lost in five sets at Roland Garros as extreme heat conditions raised questions about player safety protocols.
cards.body:
Jannik Sinner lost to Juan Manuel Cerúndolo of Argentina 3-6, 2-6, 7-5, 6-1, 6-1 in the second round of the French Open on Thursday. The world No. 1 described the defeat as "tough to accept" given his current form and ranking.

Sinner attributed his loss to illness rather than extreme heat conditions at the tournament. He plans to skip grass-court events before Wimbledon and take time to recover both physically and mentally.

cards.headline: Thunder's Jalen Williams, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander struggle in Game 6 loss
cards.teaser: Williams scored just one point in his return from injury while Gilgeous-Alexander finished well below his season average.
cards.body:
Jalen Williams managed just one point in his return from a hamstring injury as the Oklahoma City Thunder fell to the San Antonio Spurs 118-91 in Game 6 of the Western Conference finals. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander also struggled, scoring well below his regular-season average in the loss.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with 28 points and 10 rebounds, powering San Antonio past elimination and forcing a Game 7 in the series.

cards.headline: Knicks center Mitchell Robinson suffers broken finger before NBA Finals
cards.teaser: Robinson broke his right pinkie finger with no timetable for return as New York prepares for the championship series.
cards.body:
New York Knicks center Mitchell Robinson has suffered a broken right pinkie finger ahead of the NBA Finals, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. The team has not provided a timetable for his return to action.

The injury comes at a critical time as the Knicks prepare for the championship series, creating significant uncertainty around Robinson's availability for the Finals matchup.

cards.headline: Aces coach Becky Hammon criticizes officiating after loss to Wings
cards.teaser: Hammon said her team is not getting the same whistle after three stars combined for one free throw attempt.
cards.body:
Las Vegas Aces coach Becky Hammon criticized the officiating following her team's 95-87 loss to the Dallas Wings on Thursday. Hammon said she is tired of the free throw disparity her team faces, noting that A'ja Wilson, Chennedy Carter and Jackie Young combined for just one free throw attempt.

Hammon stated the Aces are not getting the same whistle as their opponents. The coach's comments highlighted her frustration with what she perceives as inconsistent officiating affecting her team's ability to get to the free throw line.

cards.headline: Nebraska extends winning streak to 27 with walk-off homer at Women's College World Series
cards.teaser: Ava Kuszak hit a game-winning home run in the 10th inning to beat Arkansas in the opening round.
cards.body:
Ava Kuszak hit a game-winning home run in the 10th inning to lead Nebraska past Arkansas on Thursday night in the Women's College World Series opening round. The walk-off blast extended the Cornhuskers' winning streak to 27 games, the longest active streak in college baseball.

The victory gave Nebraska a dramatic start to the tournament as they continue their dominant season run.

hero.headline: A24 Horror Film 'Backrooms' Opens With $9 Million in Thursday Previews
hero.body:
A24's horror film Backrooms earned $9 million in Thursday night preview screenings, surpassing the preview performance of Scream 7. The film was directed by 20-year-old Kane Parsons.

The preview total puts Backrooms ahead of the previous Scream franchise entry in terms of early box office performance. Preview screenings typically take place the evening before a film's official wide release and serve as an early indicator of audience interest.

Parsons, who is two decades old, helmed the feature film for A24, the studio known for horror releases including Hereditary, Midsommar, and X. The film has received attention for its atmospheric approach and unsettling visual style.

Early critical response has focused on the film's tone and visual design. Reviews have described Backrooms as an atmospheric experience that creates disorientation through its environment. Critics have noted the film's approach to building tension through its setting and presentation.

The film takes its name and concept from an internet phenomenon describing endless maze-like office spaces. The Backrooms originated as an online horror concept featuring empty fluorescent-lit rooms and corridors that became a viral cultural reference point.

Parsons gained recognition for creating Backrooms content on YouTube before transitioning to the feature film format. His earlier short-form videos exploring the Backrooms concept built an audience online and demonstrated his visual style.

The $9 million preview total represents a strong start for an original horror property not based on an established franchise. Horror films have historically performed well in preview screenings when they generate word-of-mouth interest among genre audiences.

The film's official wide release follows the preview screenings. Box office analysts will watch the weekend totals to determine whether the preview momentum translates into sustained ticket sales across multiple days.

cards.headline: Martina McBride Withdraws From Trump-Linked America's 250th Anniversary Concerts
cards.teaser: Country singer Martina McBride joined several performers in canceling appearances at the Freedom 250 concert series in Washington.
cards.body:
Country music performer Martina McBride withdrew from the Great American State Fair concert series tied to former President Trump. The concerts were planned as part of celebrations marking America's 250th anniversary in Washington.

Morris Day also canceled his scheduled performance at the Freedom 250 concerts. The wave of cancellations came shortly after the initial lineup was announced, reducing the roster of artists scheduled to appear at the anniversary events in the nation's capital.

cards.headline: Female Entertainers Report Sexual Harassment at Venues
cards.teaser: Performers described experiences of being groped and receiving unwanted sexual comments while working at entertainment venues.
cards.body:
Female entertainers disclosed incidents of sexual harassment they faced at work venues. The performers reported being groped and subjected to unwanted sexual comments during their professional engagements.

The accounts revealed harassment occurring at entertainment venues where the performers were working. The incidents described involve physical contact without consent and sexually inappropriate verbal remarks directed at the women during their performances or while present at the venues.

cards.headline: Anderson Cooper and Andy Cohen to Host Independence Eve Live Countdown
cards.teaser: The duo will reunite for a live broadcast on the evening before Independence Day after their annual New Year's Eve collaboration.
cards.body:
CNN hosts Anderson Cooper and Andy Cohen will team up for an Independence Eve Live countdown broadcast. The pair typically host CNN's New Year's Eve Live from Times Square each December.

The Independence Eve program marks a departure from their traditional year-end broadcast schedule. The special will air on the evening before Independence Day, bringing their familiar hosting dynamic to the summer holiday celebration.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Releases 'Hate That I Made You Love Me' From Upcoming Album
cards.teaser: The pop star released a new single as the first preview of her eighth studio album titled Petal.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande released a new song called Hate That I Made You Love Me. The track represents the first single from her forthcoming eighth studio album.

The upcoming album is titled Petal. Grande's new release follows her previous seven studio albums spanning her career as a pop vocalist.

cards.headline: Bebe Rexha and David Guetta Release 'Sad Girls' Single
cards.teaser: The collaboration will appear on Rexha's album Dirty Blonde, scheduled for release in June.
cards.body:
Bebe Rexha teamed up with DJ and producer David Guetta for a new single titled Sad Girls. The song features Rexha's vocals over Guetta's production.

The track will be included on Rexha's forthcoming album Dirty Blonde. The album is scheduled for release in June, adding to Rexha's catalog of pop and dance collaborations.

cards.headline: Amazon's 'Project Hail Mary' Wins Five Golden Trailer Awards
cards.teaser: The film's marketing campaign took top honors including Best in Show at the annual advertising awards ceremony.
cards.body:
Amazon MGM's Project Hail Mary dominated the Golden Trailer Awards, taking home five prizes at the ceremony held in Beverly Hills. The film's trailer, titled "Chance" and created by Wild Card Creative Group, earned the prestigious Best in Show award.

The film also won in the Best Drama, Best Fantasy/Adventure, and Best Music categories. The Golden Trailer Awards celebrate outstanding achievement in film and television marketing and promotional materials.

hero.headline: Former Attorney General Pam Bondi to testify on Epstein files release
hero.teaser: The House Oversight Committee has scheduled testimony from Pam Bondi about her handling of Jeffrey Epstein documents.
hero.body:
Pam Bondi is scheduled to answer questions from the House Oversight Committee on Friday about how she handled the release of the Jeffrey Epstein files. The hearing comes after Bondi was removed from her position as attorney general.

The committee will question Bondi specifically about her decisions regarding the Epstein document release, though the hearing differs from what some lawmakers had sought. The testimony represents another appearance before Congress for Bondi following her departure from the Justice Department.

cards.headline: Karen Bass faces challenges from Spencer Pratt and Nithya Raman in Los Angeles mayoral primary
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles mayoral primary pits incumbent Karen Bass against a conservative reality TV star and a progressive council member.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass is defending her position in the upcoming mayoral primary against two frontrunning challengers representing different political directions. Conservative reality TV star Spencer Pratt and progressive city council member Nithya Raman offer contrasting visions for the city's future.

Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel has criticized Pratt's candidacy, comparing his campaign to Donald Trump's rise and suggesting the reality TV star is running to regain media attention rather than serve the city.

cards.headline: White House creates website displaying immigration arrest data with space theme
cards.teaser: The administration launched a website Thursday featuring arrest information for immigrants living in the US without authorization.
cards.body:
White House launches 'aliens' site touting immigrant arrests

The White House unveiled a space-themed website displaying data on arrests of undocumented immigrants. The site features a text crawl reminiscent of Star Wars films.

The launch plays on the concept of government secrecy around alleged alien encounters while simultaneously publicizing immigration enforcement actions. The space-themed format represents a new approach to presenting immigration arrest statistics through entertainment-style presentation.

cards.headline: Texas Democratic Rep. James Talarico to face Ken Paxton in Senate race
cards.teaser: The Texas primary results set up a November contest between State Rep. James Talarico and Attorney General Ken Paxton.
cards.body:
Texas State Democratic Representative James Talarico will face Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton in the race for a Senate seat after the primary solidified the matchup. NPR interviewed Talarico following the primary results.

The November election will pit Talarico, a state legislator, against Paxton, who currently serves as Texas Attorney General. The primary concluded with both candidates securing their respective party nominations for the Senate contest.

cards.headline: American savings rate drops to 2.6 percent in April
cards.teaser: The personal savings rate fell below 3 percent for the first time since mid-2022.
cards.body:
Americans saved 2.6 percent of their income in April, marking the first time the savings rate has fallen below 3 percent since June 2022. The decline represents a continued decrease in the amount of income households are setting aside.

The savings rate measures the percentage of disposable income that Americans save rather than spend. The April figure continues a downward trend in household savings behavior over recent months.

cards.headline: Pro-Israel groups spend nearly 8 million dollars against Rep. Thomas Massie in Kentucky primary
cards.teaser: Pro-Israel organizations contributed to what became the most expensive House primary in American history.
cards.body:
Pro-Israel groups spent nearly 8 million dollars to oppose GOP Representative Thomas Massie in Kentucky's 4th District primary. The spending helped fuel what became the most expensive House primary race in American history.

The investment represents part of a broader trend of issue-focused organizations spending substantial sums in congressional races. AI companies, the cryptocurrency industry, and pro-Israel groups are all increasing their political expenditures to influence which candidates win office.

cards.headline: Martina McBride withdraws from America 250 concert on National Mall
cards.teaser: The country singer said she was misled about the nature of the July event celebrating the nation's 250th birthday.
